claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A transformer pre-trained on broad alloy data and fine-tuned on experimental data can predict mechanical properties of HEAs.
The proposed model can accurately predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Large, diverse HEA and binary or multicomponent alloy datasets are suitable pre-training data for the proposed model.
Fine-tuning with experimental tensile and fracture-property measurements can adapt the model to the target properties.
Self-attention can encode the multiscale chemical fluctuations of the HfNbTiVAl10 hierarchical heterostructure.
Attention weights constitute a representation of the alloy's physical multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Transformer self-attention captures composition-dependent elemental interactions relevant to alloy properties.
Self-attention can correlate heterogeneous chemical fluctuations at multiple length scales with macroscopic mechanical properties.
Once pre-trained, the transformer can screen alloys without the extensive computational resources required by DFT.
The proposed model will reduce computational cost by at least three orders of magnitude.
The proposed model will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 10–20% relative to CALPHAD and first-principles methods.
Pre-training and transfer learning mitigate HEA data scarcity and improve data efficiency.
Pre-trained transformers outperform random forests and Gaussian processes for elongation and ultimate tensile strength prediction.
The model should remain reliable at room temperature and moderate strain rates when the tested behavior is represented by the training data.
The model may cease to be reliable when processing-induced microstructures or heterogeneities fall outside the pre-training or fine-tuning domain.
The exact accuracy and efficiency gains depend on training-data representativeness and the degree of microstructural variation.
